provenance.git_rev_note: read-only 'git rev-parse --short HEAD' run from the script for provenance only -- the single git operation the E7 task permits; 'unavailable' when git cannot run

seeds.role: each experiment seed rotates onto a stream composition (seed % 3) and drives its own deterministic draw of unseen cases
seeds.unseen_draw_rng: random.Random('e7-replay-generalization-seed{seed}') -- recorded draw order, stable across runs
seeds.multi_seed_note: five seeds by default (task discipline); the per-seed agreement rates are aggregated to mean/stdev by this script from the raw rows

provenance.oracle: per case, the recorded constituent sequence is re-run from scratch via record_trace with the unseen values as the initial shared context and the step outputs are merged; the learned composite's replay result must equal that merged dict exactly (per-case exact equality, no tolerance)

conventions.wrapped: {'ctx': {<params>}} -- the run_stream convention the mining traces were recorded under
conventions.sibling: {'ctx': {}, <params>} -- schema parameters passed alongside an empty ctx (the sibling-binding path I6 added)

provenance.determinism: the unseen draws, mining, replay and oracle are deterministic functions of the experiment seeds; only generated_at_utc and git_rev vary between runs; every aggregate is computed by this script from the raw per-case rows published in 'cases'
provenance.cases_row_schema: [seed, case_idx, <one value per composition param, in template.params order>, convention_idx, match(0/1), empty_kept(0/1), error(0/1)]; convention names are ('wrapped', 'flat', 'sibling')[convention_idx]

experiment.question: Does a learned composite instruction, mined from traces that recorded only a small grid of parameter values, replay exactly like re-running its recorded constituent sequence for parameter values never observed during mining?
method: per experiment seed, mine one composite template from traces of a multi-operator stream recorded over its recorded parameter grid (the only values mining sees)
draw N >= 200 unseen parameter combinations per seed from ranges disjoint from the recorded grid: per-coordinate disjoint, unique, never a recorded tuple

for each unseen case, execute the learned instruction under a rotating calling convention and compare its result for exact equality against re-running the recorded constituent sequence with the same values
aggregate per-seed agreement rates to mean/stdev; publish the raw per-case rows alongside every aggregate

conventions.wrapped: {'ctx': {<params>}} -- the run_stream convention the mining traces were recorded under
conventions.sibling: {'ctx': {}, <params>} -- schema parameters passed alongside an empty ctx (the sibling-binding path I6 added)

experiment.streams_note: synthetic deterministic integer pipelines (mod-97 arithmetic) over the run_stream ctx convention: every step reads the shared ctx and merges its dict outputs back; the replayed operators are pure and stateless

components_required: I6-replay-parameterization: learned composite replay + saved parameter schema + sibling binding (all shipped per its implementation report; this benchmark only ran because they are)
measured: per-case exact-equality agreement of learned composite replay vs oracle re-run on unseen parameter values (the headline)
empty-result edge coverage (kept == [] cases, counted in n_empty_kept_total)
unseen-ness guards (per-coordinate disjoint, unique tuples, no recorded tuple reused, per-seed minimum)
not_covered: dialogue-mined templates with an attached executor (I6's other arm): out of scope -- no recorded composite body to re-run, nothing to compare

constructor-bound parameters (values baked into instruction state at construction time): replay re-runs the recorded instances, so only ctx-carried values can vary (I6 deviation 1); the streams here read every parameter from ctx

real-workload / LLM streams: the measured streams are deterministic synthetic arithmetic; the claim measured is exact per-case equality on this domain, not a distributional claim about arbitrary workloads

schema-violating values: recorded honestly as error cases by the harness (pinned by the test suite) but deliberately absent from the committed run's denominator, which replays only type-valid unseen values
